narrative.overview: A pale blue chart of the county fills the room; clear glass instruments rest on it and bend the map beneath them. The map is the workspace and never recedes behind chrome. Residents get the same chart under the same glass, made denser where they read.
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed map, panels float on it.
One material, two densities: full liquid glass for staff panels and top pills; denser, non-refracting glass for resident reading panels.
Round tokens carry meaning on the map.
Thin, large numerals for readings; small mono for codes and times.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Outside an AQI chip, orange means a person is requesting help. Actions are blue.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: All figures use tabular numerals so columns of readings line up.

rules.name: The Overview Chart Rule
rules.body: The resident chart is a still overview: no pan, no zoom, no controls; only sites inside San Diego County are drawn or counted.

dos: Do keep the map visible behind and between panels.
Do keep text on glass at Navy Ink or Ink 2; check contrast where the map shows through.
Do pair every status color with a word or number.
Do label mock data wherever it appears.
Do keep resident tap targets at 56px or taller.
donts: Don't use orange for anything but a person requesting help, except inside an AQI chip.
Don't put refracting (#liquid) or thin glass behind resident reading text; resident panels use the denser reading glass.
Don't add colored glow shadows or violet.
Don't show a caller's name or phone number; location and stated needs only.
Don't present a discovered site the same way as an official one.
